title: Reverse and count anything
description:
Write two functions that work on arrays of any element type:

```c
void reverse_any(void *base, size_t n, size_t size);
size_t count_if(const void *base, size_t n, size_t size, int (*pred)(const void *item));
```

- `reverse_any` reverses the order of the `n` elements of `size` bytes each, in place. Elements may be up to 256 bytes.
- `count_if` returns how many elements `pred` returns non-zero for.
hints: Step through the bytes with `unsigned char *b = base;`: element `i` starts at `b + i * size` (lesson 8.02).
Swap two elements with `memcpy` through a temporary buffer; stop when the two indexes meet.
